newsitem.title: UK: Unilever Q2 profit to rise, eyes on volume.
newsitem.headline: Unilever Q2 profit to rise, eyes on volume.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch foods and consumer products group Unilever NV/Plc is likely to report higher second quarter profits on August 1 but exceptionals will keep the focus on underlying volume growth and margins, analysts said.
"The message is likely to be that underlying performance is still good, we will also be looking for continuing margin improvement," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
Analysts are expecting pre-tax profits to come in at between 720 and 780 million stg on a constant exchange rate basis for the second quarter, compared with 616 million previously.
Recent strength of the pound could be reflected in results, analysts said.
European margins are expected to build on the improvement seen in the first quarter, as the benefits of restructuring continue to come through, analysts said.

In the U.S., profits are expected to show an increase over the same period of last year, turning around the 11 percent fall seen in the first quarter, which was hampered by flat markets and a high marketing spend.
For the rest of the world, Unilever is expected to see good volume growth in most markets, analysts said.
Analysts will also be looking for indications on investments after Unilever sold its international specialty chemicals business to Britain's ICI for a debt-free price of $8 billion in May.
"I think there could be more information next week on how that will impact in the short-term. Longer-term depends on how they invest," the analyst said.
Any possible acquisitions are expected to be in fields where the company is already operating, analysts said, as it tries to increase critical mass.
Emerging markets could also prove a magnet for investments, they added, as organic growth could be strongest here.
